hero.name: Natã.
hero.bio: I build complete web applications - from the interface to business rules and integrations. I care about code that still makes sense months later, and products that hold up in the real world, not just the happy path.

about.label: About me
about.titleAccent: curious about both sides of the app.
about.lead: I like understanding how things work on both sides of the application. I might be refining a React interface one moment and modeling a business rule or backend integration the next.
about.p1Before: I've spent more than three years building for the web. In that time I've worked with
about.p1After: on applications that had to work for real: authentication, third-party integrations, REST APIs and responsive interfaces that stand up to actual use.
about.p2: I've shipped event management systems, payment gateways, reservation flows, registration and check-in. I've learned that the hard part is almost never writing the code - it's understanding the problem well enough not to write too much of it.
about.p3: I started in support and infrastructure, and I think that left a mark: I like knowing what sits under the abstraction. Today I'm studying Software Engineering and pulling that thread toward architecture, backend and systems closer to the hardware.

stack.label: Technologies
stack.description: No vanity logo wall - only what I actually write, maintain or study right now.

experience.label: Work experience
experience.description: A fairly straight line: I started fixing what already existed, moved into building for the web, and today I work on both ends of the application.

projects.label: Projects

education.label: Education and languages
education.note: I read docs, articles and code in English every day - that's where the information arrives first.

colophon.metaDescription: How this portfolio was made - stack, intro, i18n, theme, and the decisions behind the site.
colophon.lead: Not a changelog. A map of the decisions that matter - the ones you see and the ones that try to stay invisible.
colophon.source: The source for this site lives at {repo} on
colophon.snippetCaption: The intro waits for the globe. The draw starts when WebGL says so - or when the ten-second cap fires.

stack.title: Stack
stack.body: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind v4. Motion for transitions, Three.js for the globe, next-intl for pt/en. Theming via @wrksz/themes so React 19 doesn't fight an inline script.

intro.title: The intro
intro.body: The logo draws, flies to the header, then the rest comes in. The 3D globe warms up backstage - if it stalled mid-animation, you'd notice. That's why the wait happens before the draw, not during it.

i18n.title: Two languages, one address
i18n.body: Portuguese is the default at /. English lives at /en. Section hashes (#sobre, #projetos) stay stable so shared links don't break. On the first visit, the locale follows the browser.

theme.title: Light and dark
theme.body: Semantic tokens, no flash. The theme script lands in the HTML before paint; React doesn't need to inject inline JavaScript on the client just for that.

command.title: The palette
command.body: ⌘K (or Ctrl K) opens shortcuts: sections, theme, language, email, GitHub. The kind of detail I'd hope to find on someone else's site.

type.title: Type and color
type.body: Geist Sans and Geist Mono. Electric blue in dark mode, a deeper blue in light - the same system, two moods.
